sections.title: Getting started
sections.summary: What ApolloSG does, setting it up, and finding your way around.

topics.title: What ApolloSG does
topics.answer: ApolloSG helps protect you from scams and online threats. Apollo watches and checks things for you, TC Hawkeye and Magnum DI investigate anything that needs a closer look, and Higgins explains what was found and shows you where to go.

details.heading: Who does what
details.text:
• Apollo — the watchdog. Watches, checks, blocks and records what happens on this device.
• TC Hawkeye — Apollo's quick investigator. Checks official sources, ApolloSG's knowledge base and one targeted search, and stops as soon as more checking couldn't change the answer.
• Magnum DI — the deep investigator. Called in only when TC Hawkeye can't settle something and a deeper look could change the answer.
• Higgins — your guide. Explains results, answers questions about scams and about ApolloSG, and takes you to the right screen. Higgins doesn't investigate.

details.heading: No account needed
details.text: ApolloSG doesn't ask for your name, email address or a password. It registers this phone with an anonymous device ID.

topics.title: Setting up ApolloSG
topics.answer: Setting up takes a few minutes: read the privacy statement, turn on the protections your phone allows, then let Apollo read your device's starting point.
steps: Open ApolloSG and tap “Continue”.
Read the privacy statement, then tap “I understand — set up ApolloSG”.
ApolloSG offers each protection your phone allows, one at a time. Tap the button to turn it on, or “Not now” to skip it. “Skip the rest for now” skips the remaining ones.
Tap “Next: your first check”. Apollo reads this device's security settings — ApolloSG never assumes a new phone is clean.
When the first check finishes, you arrive on Home.

details.heading: Skipped a protection?
details.text: You can turn it on at any time later. See “Turning a protection on or fixing one”.

notes: Website protection and message screening are offered on Android only.

topics.title: Finding your way around
topics.answer: The five tabs along the bottom are Home, Threats, Ask Higgins, Alerts and Learn. Everything else is in the ☰ menu at the top right of most screens.

details.heading: The tabs
details.text:
• Home — Apollo's status, your protection and anything that needs you.
• Threats — every case Apollo has opened, with its full details.
• Ask Higgins — ask a question, or tap ⊕ to have something checked.
• Alerts — current scam warnings from official sources (called Scam Alerts on tablets).
• Learn — articles about scams and staying safe (called Learn with Higgins on tablets).

details.heading: The ☰ menu
details.text: Sample checks, User Guide, Settings, About ApolloSG, How Apollo checks, Privacy and Support.

details.heading: Other buttons you'll see
details.text:
• The bell opens your alerts: device settings that need attention, threats Apollo detected and alerts ApolloSG sent you.
• ⓘ explains the screen you're on.
• A number on the Threats tab shows how many cases need you. A number on the Alerts tab shows new serious scam alerts.

topics.title: What Apollo's states mean
topics.answer: Apollo shows how concerned he is by how he behaves: Patrolling means nothing of concern was found, Growling a possible concern, Barking a significant concern, and Biting means a real block was confirmed.

details.heading: Every state
details.text:
• Patrolling — no concern was found in the checks that completed.
• Sniffing — checks are still running; nothing is final yet.
• Sniffing something — Apollo noticed something and is looking more closely.
• Growling — a possible concern that needs caution or more investigation.
• Barking — a significant concern that needs your attention.
• Biting — an actual block, confirmed by the device's own evidence.

topics.title: Turning a protection on or fixing one
topics.answer: Open Protections from Home, tap the area, then tap the protection. ApolloSG shows what it needs and a button to fix it — often opening the right page in your phone's settings.
steps: On Home, tap “Your protection”.
On the “Apollo Protections” tab, tap the area — for example Messages & Calls.
Tap the protection you want to turn on or fix.
Follow the button ApolloSG shows, then check again to confirm it's working.

details.heading: What each protection needs
details.text:
• Website protection (Android) — permission to run a private on-device VPN filter. Your browsing isn't sent anywhere.
• Message screening (Android) — notification access. Apollo reads each new message notification as it arrives, never your SMS inbox.
• Call screening — on Android, choose ApolloSG as your Caller ID & spam app. On iPhone, turn ApolloSG on in the iPhone Settings app under Phone → Call Blocking & Identification.
• Email monitoring — connect Gmail with read-only access.

details.heading: Another way in
details.text: ☰ → Settings → Protection → “View all protections” lists every protection with its status and setup.

notes: Website protection and message screening are Android only.

topics.title: What happens after you submit something
topics.answer: Apollo's rules check it first. If they settle it, you get the answer straight away; if not, TC Hawkeye investigates, and Magnum DI looks deeper only when that could change the answer.

details.heading: While it's being checked
details.text: Progress shows in Ask Higgins. Magnum DI may ask you one question — answer it in the message box.

details.heading: The result
details.text: You'll see the findings, how sure Apollo is and what to do next. If Apollo's rules find a threat, a Threat Case opens in Threats.

details.heading: Follow-up questions
details.text: Ask about the result in the message box. Higgins answers from the finished findings — a finished investigation isn't reopened. To check something new, start a new check.

details.heading: Where results are kept
details.text: The findings are saved on this device. ApolloSG's server copy is cleaned up within 24 hours, and you can still read the saved findings afterwards. “Clear this investigation” removes it.

topics.title: Sharing something into ApolloSG
topics.answer: In the app where you see it, tap Share and choose ApolloSG. ApolloSG shows what it received and waits for you to confirm before checking anything.
steps: Open the message, link, email, screenshot or file in the app you're using.
Tap Share.
Choose ApolloSG from the list.
ApolloSG opens “Shared with ApolloSG” and says what it looks like — for example “Looks like a link”.
Tap “Check as …” to check it. If ApolloSG guessed wrong, pick another option under “Not that? Check it as…”.

details.heading: Which app it arrived in
details.text: For a message, ApolloSG asks which app it arrived in, so your case shows where it came from. Tap the app, or “I'm not sure — check it anyway”.

details.heading: What you can share
details.text: Text and chat messages, links, emails (including .eml email files), pictures and files — several files at once, too.

topics.answer: Not every app offers Share for every kind of item. When ApolloSG isn't listed, copy and paste the item into a check, or take a screenshot and check that instead.

details.text:
• Share works with the installed ApolloSG app, not a browser version.

• Try sharing a different way — some apps let you share a link but not a message, or the other way round.

topics.answer: Threats lists every case Apollo has opened for you — blocked links, suspicious messages, calls and investigations. Tap any case to see its full details.

details.heading: Filter and sort
details.text: Use the filter button to show All, Investigating, Blocked, Resolved or No threat. The sort button switches between Latest first, Oldest first and Strongest evidence.

details.heading: Also on Threats
details.text: The line under the title shows when Apollo last checked. “Patrol history” is the full record of what Apollo has done; “Family alerts” shows alerts from family members you watch. The number on the Threats tab is how many cases need you.

topics.title: Reading a Threat Case
topics.answer: Tap a case in Threats to open its Threat Case. “Findings Brief” explains what happened and what to do, “Evidence” shows what ApolloSG received, and “History” shows each step in order.

details.heading: The tabs
details.text:
• Findings Brief — what Apollo found, why it matters and what to do next.
• Evidence — the original item as it arrived, and what was checked.
• History — each step, in order.
• DI — Magnum DI's full report, when Magnum DI investigated.

details.heading: What you can do
details.text: Depending on the case: “Ask Higgins to explain”, “Block this destination”, “Trust this exact link”, “Mark as contained” or “Close Case”. On the Evidence tab, “Share” sends a summary of the case and “Copy facts & sources” copies it. A closed case can be opened again with “Reopen case”.

topics.title: Family sharing
topics.answer: Family sharing lets a trusted family member who also uses ApolloSG receive your serious alerts. Set it up in ☰ → Settings → Accounts & family → “Family sharing”.

details.heading: Pairing
details.text: Create a code and give it to your family member to enter in their app. A code works once and expires after 15 minutes.

details.text: Your Barking and Biting alerts appear in their app, plus a calm weekly check-in — how many things Apollo checked and how many alerts — never what you checked.

sections.title: Privacy and your data
sections.summary: What ApolloSG keeps, your personal details and deleting your data.

topics.title: What ApolloSG keeps and shares
topics.answer: ApolloSG has no account, no advertising tracking and needs no email address. Checks start on your phone, and only what an assessment needs is sent — for that one assessment.

details.heading: Key facts
details.text:
• An anonymous device ID instead of an account.
• Passwords, verification codes and the secret parts of links are removed before anything is sent.
• Cases keep a summary and safe references, not full messages, screenshots or files.
• Background access — like message screening or a connected mailbox — each needs its own opt-in.

details.heading: Read more
details.text: ☰ → Privacy explains the principles. Settings → “Privacy statement” lists exactly what leaves your phone and when. Settings → “What ApolloSG stores” shows everything ApolloSG holds.

sections.title: Android and iPhone
sections.summary: What works on each kind of phone.

topics.title: Android and iPhone differences
topics.answer: Every manual check works on both Android and iPhone. Some automatic protections depend on what the phone allows: website protection and message screening are Android only.

details.heading: Android only
details.text:
• Website protection — a private on-device VPN filter that blocks known dangerous websites.
• Message screening — checks new message notifications as they arrive.
• Picking from your installed apps, recent messages or recent callers, where ApolloSG offers it.

details.heading: Calls
details.text: On Android, ApolloSG can screen incoming calls once you choose it as your Caller ID & spam app. On iPhone, Apple doesn't let apps check calls as they ring; once you turn ApolloSG on under Phone → Call Blocking & Identification, it can block numbers you've blocked or that are known high-risk.

details.heading: On both
details.text: Checks in Ask Higgins, sharing into ApolloSG, Threats, Scam Alerts, Learn, Family sharing and connecting Gmail.

topics.answer: Open Protections from Home, then tap the area and the protection. ApolloSG explains what's wrong and shows a button to fix it.
